sentences.text: , the applicant preferred an appeal (Criminal Appeal Case No.22/2022) before the Sessions Judge, Bemetara (C.G.)., which has been dismissed by the impugned judgment dated 22-07-2023 and upheld the conviction and sentence of the applicants.
Hence, this revision.
Learned counsel appearing for the applicants submit that the applicants were on bail during trial.
The applicants have not misused the bail granted to them.
Counsel for applicant submit that as per PW-26 Yeswant Dilliwar, an agreement was executed.
They submits that even the victim Luvkush has stated that he has not sold his land to anyone and his property is in his possession.
This witness has also stated that he has not suffered any loss.
Counsel for applicants submit that one motorcycle has been seized from applicant Naresh Kumar Jaiswal and Rs.1,000/- has been seized from applicant Bhanwar Lal.
They submit that the wife of applicant Naresh Kumar is pregnant.

They further submit that the main accused has already been released on bail by this Court vide order dated 22.08.2023 in CRR No. 871/2023 and final hearing of these revisions is likely to take considerable time, hence, the substantive jail sentence imposed upon applicants may be suspended till the disposal of these revisions.

On the other hand, learned State counsel vehemently opposing the submission made by counsel for applicants submits that the present applicants impersonating one of them as the victim Luvkush and preparing forged Rinpustika got the land of victim sold to someone else.
He further submits that the report of handwriting expert has also come and considering the nature of offence, the applicants do not deserve to be released on bail.
Heard the submission and perused the impugned order.

Considering the entire facts and circumstances of the case particularly the fact that the main accused has already been granted bail by this Court in CRR 871/2023 and final hearing of these revisions is likely to take considerable time, I am inclined to allow I.A. No.01/2023 in all the three revisions.
It is directed that the execution of substantive jail sentence imposed on the present applicants shall remain suspended during the pendency of these revisions and they shall be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.25,000/- with one surety each in the like sum to the satisfaction of the trial Court.

The applicants shall appear before the Registry of this Court on 29.09.2023 and thereafter they shall appear before the trial Court on a date to be given by the Bhanwar Lal vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105824414/
